Reported busy season Seasonal variation in workload has direct implications for hiring and training. Contractors may be more likely to seek additional workers or invest in training ahead of anticipated busy periods, whereas slower seasons may offer more flexibility for staff to attend off-site or classroom-based training. 4.3 Hiring Practices Reasons Companies Start Hiring Contractors reported a range of motivations for bringing on new workers, with quality, staffing needs, and business growth all playing central roles. The five most common reasons contractors cited for hiring a worker were: to keep quality high (73%), to replace someone who left (70%), to secure a great candidate (64%), to increase profits (63%), and to keep up with new business (61%). Top five reasons respondents hire new workers These findings suggest that hiring decisions are often closely tied to multiple factors, primarily related to growth, employee turnover, and the objective of maintaining or improving work quality. The top response indicates that contractors are primarily driven by a commitment to producing high-quality work on their projects. This is also shown by the responses about hiring when “a great candidate is found,” highlighting that contractors also hire even when they do not have vacancies; they seize opportunities when attractive candidates who can add value to their work become available. This suggests that increasing the number of well-trained workers and fostering connections between qualified job seekers and contractors can spur hiring and encourage contractors to grow their businesses. This is a crucial finding for workforce development and training programs, as it may indicate a need to expand programming beyond technical training to focus on connecting contractors with trainees and program graduates. Additionally, employee turnover is a significant factor in hiring. This may mean that hiring activity does not always correlate with company growth but may simply reflect replacing workers who have separated. Nevertheless, in line with the high percentage of respondents who indicated a desire to grow their companies in the previous section, a high number of respondents hire because “more employees mean more profit,” because their “company has new business,” or because of new rebates or tax credits. This reflects a growth-oriented mindset, where contractors respond to demand signals and actively seek to increase revenue rather than simply responding to staffing needs.
